transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-06 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~90 min | Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Patel, Jordan Miles, Anika Rao, Ben Torres

Summary (auto): quick internal lab to tighten demo narrative and safety fallback language; roleplay + playbook edits. Links: internal playbook https://intra.redwood/playbooks/conversational-framework (note: repo preview); recording will be posted.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya: alright everyone, thanks for joining the lab, uh, we'll kick off at 4 pm. quick note, this is internal only. we'll do intro, two short roleplays, then capture edits to the two minute script.
[00:22] Liam: hey—hi, team. quick housekeeping, the key thing I want us to practice is the safety flow, so when model does something weird in demo, the words to use, and the fallback to dedicated/private if customer needs it.
[00:37] Jordan: sounds good. can we also include a line for performance — like if a customer asks about latency vs cost, what do we say? that's, like, the most common kicker.
[00:48] Priya: yeah we'll script a couple of variants, high-level and technical. high-level: "we optimize for predictable latency with dedicated capacity; hosted for speed to value." technical: mention batching, KV cache, and quantization. but say kv cache, not kv cash — haha.
[01:05] Anika: (laughs) noted. also can someone remind me which models we are allowed to demo live in hosted? is there a whitelist?
[01:12] Liam: short answer: yes, there is a curated catalog. we present Redwood-verified profiles; anything experimental we sandbox locally or use a recorded transcript. we should avoid live unsafe generation in prospect demos.
[01:24] Ben: can we add a line about customer data — like, "we don't persist customer inputs on hosted by default"? legal keeps asking.
[01:31] Maya: good call. include the privacy blurb: hosted has ephemeral inputs, retained only for diagnostics if authorized; for enterprise we offer Private with KMS and audit logs. keep it short.
[01:42] [Roleplay 1 setup — Jordan plays skeptical platform lead, Maya is AE, Liam is SE persona behind the demo]
[01:47] Jordan: ok Maya, show me a quick gen use case. convince me it's safe.
[01:51] Maya: sure—let's do a quick customer support snippet. "Redwood can summarize incoming threads and suggest actions while keeping customer data isolated. here's a brief sample." (reads) "Customer: I need refund; Agent:..."
[02:05] Jordan: stop — pause — the output looks like it pulled an internal name there, how do we prevent leakage?
[02:10] Liam: yes this is the teachable moment: mention prefix-level caching and redaction heuristics, and that during demos we use sanitized prompts. if a customer needs no outside network, we move to private or dedicated.
[02:22] Maya: script line: "We sanitize demo inputs and have redaction rules; for regulated data we recommend Redwood Private with KMS and full audit logs."
[02:32] Jordan: that's better. shorter: "we sanitize demo inputs; for regulated data we move to Private with KMS and audit logs."
[02:38] Priya: note to add an escalation phrase: "If you want, we can run a short POC with your redacted sample data to show exact behavior."
[02:46] Anika: can we also add a fallback if the model hallucinates in front of a buyer — like, immediately switch to a canned transcript?
[02:52] Liam: yes, two options: 1) swap to a recorded transcript and say "we recorded this to show expected output"; 2) switch to a smaller, deterministic model variant. mention both.
[03:03] Maya: ok here's the 2-minute demo draft based on that: "Hi — in two minutes: problem, Redwood approach, demo of sanitized flow, performance note, next step POC." read-through, then we all tweak.
[03:16] [Timestamp jump — discussion of exact wording and cadence, edits noted]
[03:45] Liam: quick technical micro-script: "we route requests with smart routing that can prefer dedicated GPU pools for SLOs; continuous batching reduces per-token cost; KV cache avoids recomputation for conversational contexts." watch for jargon overload.
[03:58] Ben: that sentence loses leadership — marketing wants a one-liner: "predictable latency through reserved capacity and intelligent request routing."
[04:07] Maya: agree. we'll have the technical addendum for SE chats. main script: keep it punchy.
[04:15] [Roleplay 2 — buyer asks about migration from another provider who does embeddings cheaply]
[04:20] Jordan (buyer): we've been using another vendor for embeddings and they're cheaper. why switch?
[04:25] Maya: response: "cheaper per-unit isn't the full picture — we help teams cut unit costs via batching, caching, and model selection while improving tail latency and reliability; plus better operational tooling and rollout controls."
[04:40] Jordan: buyer asks for hard numbers.
[04:42] Liam: we should avoid committing to specific $ numbers unless it's a customer benchmark; instead offer to run a cost/perf POC or share our public benchmark. say: "we'll run a quick benchmark on your workload and show projected unit economics."
[04:56] Maya: phrase it as commitment: "we'll run a scoped POC to show economics on your dataset" — that tends to win.
[05:02] Anika: when should AE escalate to SE for performance deep dives?
[05:06] Priya: rule of thumb: if customer asks for <200ms p95 or mentions on-prem constraints, involve SE. also if they ask about certifications like SOC2/ISO or data residency.
[05:20] Ben: note for playbook: include checklist for escalation with example language.
[05:25] [Mid-call pause — quick break then reconvene]
[05:40] Maya: back. next segment — demo handoff choreography. how does AE start and how does SE jump in without derailing flow?
[05:46] Liam: handoff script: "I'll step in to demo technical aspects; I'll highlight routing and fallback policies" followed by a prepped line: "If you'd like, I can show the private deployment option and audit logs."
[05:58] Jordan: we practiced that — remember to keep time: AE owns first 60 seconds, SE 30 sec highlight, AE close.
[06:08] Priya: we timed the trimmed script at 1:40 earlier — that's ideal. keep to the rhythm.
[06:14] [Timestamps extend — group tries alternate phrasings, some cross talk] 
[06:38] Jordan: sometimes buyers object with vendor lock-in concerns — what's the response?
[06:42] Liam: talk about model and deployment portability, mention you can pin model versions and have rollbacks; highlight open model catalog and that customers can export artifacts. avoid saying "not locked" — instead say "we provide standard export formats and clear migration paths."
[06:58] Maya: also point to SDKs and infra templates to lower migration cost.
[07:05] Anika: question: do we ever demo quantized models live?
[07:09] Liam: generally no for external demos — show perf numbers or a recorded demo. quantization details go in SE appendix.
[07:17] Ben: marketing wants a simple line about cost controls: "We recommend quantization and batch configs for most production NLP workloads to lower unit costs without sacrificing quality." fine.
[07:27] [Exercise: objection ladder — team practices three escalation lines for cost/latency/security]
[07:31] Maya: final check — who will own updating the playbook after this call?
[07:34] Priya: I will. I'll fold in the two-minute script, the escalation checklist, and the roleplay excerpts.
[07:40] Jordan: also can we create short GIFs of the safe-demo flow for enablement docs? quick visual help.
[07:46] Maya: good idea. Anika can capture.
[07:49] Anika: yep I'll record the two roleplays and export clips.
[07:52] [Closing recap]
[07:55] Maya: recap: Maya to send 2-min script + recording; Priya to update playbook; Liam to produce sample prompt/perf notes; Jordan to schedule roleplay follow-up. Next session week of 2025-05-19.
[08:10] Ben: thanks all. one last tip — always prep a deterministic sample if you're demoing hallucination-prone flows.
[08:16] Maya: noted. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: some words auto-corrected, names and product nouns may be inconsistent (KV cache vs KV cash, Redwood Private phrasing), filler words present.
